title: [CQ-R13f] Certify writer and check containment probes
definitionOfDone: 'writer-containment' passes only when every agent-identity probe is refused: credential, root-only manifest, /opt/moe, another home, supervisor and toolchain. Any success fails the check. Shown by tests.

'check-containment' passes only when the probe run passes, the protected-overwrite run resolves 'inconclusive' and the tracked-edit run resolves workspace 'changed'. Any other outcome fails the check. Shown by tests with fake runCheckJob results.

'controller-replacement' passes only when readiness refuses a replaced supervisor and this run's cleanup leaves a foreign-owned ledger record alone. It runs last among the certify-VM checks. Shown by tests.
The verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.

implementationPlan.description:
writer-containment, in scripts/local-runner/certify-bridge.mjs and scripts/local-runner/certify-containment.mjs (prototype hunks in the memory).

1. certify-bridge.mjs: export `probe` (one keyword) and name certify-containment.mjs in its comment. Its behavior is unchanged: runGuestProbe's handling, {code, stdout} for a remote exit, a PROVIDER_* throw for a kill, spawn or other provider failure.
2. certify-containment.mjs:
   - Imports: probe as guestExec, buildUserData, GUEST_LAYOUT and JOB_IDENTITIES, waitForGuestReady, deleteOwned and queryOwnedInstance, installToolchain, fetchNodeToolchain, readFile/writeFile and path (the last group is used by step 3).
   - OTHER_HOME = '/var/lib/moe/sessions/home-certify'. HOME_ARGV = ['sudo', '-n', 'install', '-d', '-m', '0700', '-o', JOB_IDENTITIES[1], '-g', JOB_IDENTITIES[1], OTHER_HOME]: another job's home, made as guest-supervisor.py session_home makes one, under a name mkdtemp never draws.
   - WRITER_TARGETS, seven [code, path, access mode] rows: CREDENTIAL GUEST_LAYOUT.credential 4; MANIFEST /var/lib/moe/workspace.manifest.json 4; CONTROL_PLANE /opt/moe 2; HOME OTHER_HOME 2; SUPERVISOR GUEST_LAYOUT.supervisor 2; TOOLCHAIN /opt/moe/toolchain/bin 2; TOOLCHAIN /opt/moe/toolchain/bin/node 2.
   - Exported WRITER_PROBE: one python line, no quote. As the agent identity it exits 10+i for the first target it may access, 20+i for one it cannot see, else 0.
   - writerContainment(c), with seam = c.deps?.writer ?? {} (test-only):
     a. The home exec; a non-zero exit is CERTIFY_WRITER_SETUP_FAILED.
     b. toolchain = (seam.toolchain ?? fetchNodeToolchain)({ arch: c.outcome?.image?.source?.arch, cacheDir: c.cacheDir }).
     c. (seam.installToolchain ?? installToolchain)({ name: c.name, toolchain, provider: c.provider, timeoutMs: c.bounds.transferMs }).
     d. `sudo -n -u <JOB_IDENTITIES[0]> python3 -I -c WRITER_PROBE`. Exit 0 passes. 10+i is CERTIFY_WRITER_<code>_ALLOWED, 20+i is CERTIFY_WRITER_TARGET_MISSING, anything else CERTIFY_WRITER_UNKNOWN.

Why this shape:
- `test -r/-w` alone cannot tell EACCES from ENOENT, so the probe stats each target first. A target that exists and that access(2) refuses is a permission refusal; absence is never evidence.
- The certify VM is provisioned with no toolchain and has no named foreign home, so both are made real first. The toolchain is the REAL pinned one through R11e1's cache and R11e2's install; check-containment's runs reuse that cache.

Error handling: toolchain, transfer and provider refusals propagate with their own stable codes through R13d's runCheck. Every argv is a fixed literal, and no guest byte reaches an argv, a code or the report.

The signatures I checked: buildUserData returns supervisorSha256/shimSha256/shimToolsSha256; installToolchain takes {name, toolchain, provider, timeoutMs}; fetchNodeToolchain takes {arch, cacheDir}; c.bounds.transferMs is 120_000 (BRIDGE_BOUNDS); certify-bridge does not import certify-containment, so there is no cycle. implementationPlan.description:
controller-replacement, the registry order, and certify.mjs comments.

scripts/local-runner/certify-containment.mjs:
1. REPLACE_ARGV = ['sudo', '-n', 'cp', '/usr/bin/true', GUEST_LAYOUT.supervisor]. cp keeps the inode, owner and mode, so only the hash changes and layout still holds.
2. controllerReplacement(c):
   a. The replace exec; a non-zero exit is CERTIFY_REPLACEMENT_NOT_REPLACED.
   b. Readiness as provisioning ran it: waitForGuestReady({ ledger: c.ledger, name: c.name, owner: c.owner, sourceImage: c.outcome.image.source, bootstrap: { supervisorSha256, shimSha256, shimToolsSha256 }, provider: c.provider, sleep: c.deps.sleep }). The digests come from buildUserData({ supervisor: c.supervisor, credential: randomBytes(32) }); its throwaway credential is never sent.
   c. bootstrapReady !== false is CERTIFY_REPLACEMENT_ACCEPTED. failures other than exactly ['SUPERVISOR_HASH_MISMATCH'] is CERTIFY_REPLACEMENT_UNKNOWN.
   d. The ledger part. file = path.join(c.ledgerDir, `${c.name}.json`). R13h's landed certify.mjs puts ledgerDir on the context; if it is absent there, use path.join(c.workDir, 'ledger'). Read the original bytes, then in try:
      - write the record back with a fresh `attempt-<32 hex>` attemptId;
      - refusal = the rejection code of (c.deps.replacement?.deleteOwned ?? deleteOwned)({ ledger: c.ledger, name: c.name, owner: c.owner, provider: c.provider }), through Promise.resolve().then(...);
      - kept = c.ledger.read(c.name), null on a throw; vm = queryOwnedInstance(c.name, c.provider), null on a throw;
      - pass only when refusal === 'LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER', kept.phase === 'owned', kept.attemptId is the rewritten one, and vm.present === true. Otherwise CERTIFY_REPLACEMENT_RECORD_NOT_KEPT.
      In finally, write the original bytes back, so teardown still deletes the VM.
3. CONTAINMENT_CHECKS = frozen { id, run } entries for 'writer-containment', 'check-containment', 'controller-replacement', in that order. Extend the header comment.

Why the certify VM's own record, not a decoy: a reserve draws deps.random and would shift every VM name R13h's rows pin (CERTIFY_DELETES, LC1, LC3, CC6), and it would leave a record for R13h's recovery to reconcile. This rewrite also shows the cleanup re-reads ownership from disk, against a real VM.

scripts/local-runner/certify.mjs, comments only:
- the header line names R13f's two checks and that controller-replacement is last on the certify VM;
- certifyCore's injected-transports list gains writer and replacement.
BODY needs no edit: it already splices CONTAINMENT_CHECKS before LIFECYCLE_CHECKS. So controller-replacement is the last check that uses the certify VM; cancellation, recovery and R13g's canary use their own VMs, and teardown stays last.

Error handling: a readFile or writeFile failure propagates as its stable code. Natively deps is {}, so no seam applies. executionReady stays false.

comments.author: architect-899a90d6
comments.content:
Architect, 2026-10-30: two decisions the human made in the architect REPL.

1. Split for size. The three checks measured about 470 changed lines, over QA's 400 cap. New prerequisite CQ-R13f1 (task-4e2ab1584c3140019be709b94c71f1cc) lands 'check-containment' in scripts/local-runner/certify-containment.mjs. This row adds 'writer-containment' before it and 'controller-replacement' after it in the same module, and its gate re-runs all three. DoD 2 is delivered by R13f1's landed bytes and re-verified here.

2. The protected-overwrite run. On a correct guest the check job can never change a protected file: CQ-R11b bind-mounts it read-only, so the job's own write fails with EROFS. 'inconclusive' (supervisor exit 80) only happens when a protected file changes during the run and the after-run hash check catches it. So in R13f1 the command tries the overwrite (refused), then waits, and once the session has started the certify host changes the file as root in the guest's own mount namespace. The run must resolve 'inconclusive', which keeps DoD 2 literal and exercises the after-run check natively. The probe run separately requires the job's own write to fail with EROFS.
